note: Target-audience segment library for pharma omnichannel activation (authored 2026-07). Behaviour-based segments (not just specialty/decile) with their likes, dislikes, preferred channels and engagement do's/don'ts -- the practitioner knowledge an omnichannel expert applies when building a channel plan. Grounded in current HCP-engagement research (Indegene HCP Digital Affinity, Viseven, industry 2025 omnichannel reports): ~84% of physicians want to maintain/increase digital interactions; ~68% cite webinars/webcasts as a primary information channel; ~78% prefer a mix of in-person and virtual; ~8 in 10 value personalized content and ~73% engage more when content is tailored. Percentages are directional industry findings, not brand-specific.

hcp_segments.name: Digital-first engager
hcp_segments.description: Prefers to pull information on their own schedule; rarely grants rep time. Often younger or high-volume, comfortable with digital tools and independent evidence review.
likes: On-demand content (email, web, portals) they control
Concise, data-dense clinical summaries and interactive visual aids
Personalized, relevant content tied to their patients
dislikes: Unscheduled rep visits and cold calls
Generic mass emails with no relevance
dos: Lead with rep-triggered but self-serve journeys (NPP-heavy)
Offer approve-once modular content personalized by specialty/patient mix
Make next-best-action a link, not a call

hcp_segments.name: Rep-dependent / relationship-led
hcp_segments.description: Values the trusted human relationship; forms decisions through in-person dialogue and peer credibility. Often established/community physicians with limited time for self-serve digital.
likes: Face-to-face detailing and trusted rep relationships
dislikes: Being pushed entirely to self-service digital
Content that ignores real-world practice constraints
dos: Anchor the plan in personal promotion (PP), digital as reinforcement
Equip reps with modular, MLR-approved leave-behinds
Follow up in-person interactions with a light digital recap

hcp_segments.name: Hybrid / remote-engager
hcp_segments.description: The largest and growing middle: rarely sees reps in person but actively opens emails, attends webinars and joins virtual details. Wants a coordinated mix, not one channel.
likes: Webinars/webcasts as a primary learning channel
dislikes: Disjointed channels repeating the same message
dos: Orchestrate PP+NPP with a single message architecture
Use engagement signals to pick the next channel
donts: Don't duplicate the same asset everywhere

hcp_segments.name: KOL / academic expert
hcp_segments.description: Shapes peers, guidelines and standards of care. Motivated by science, data depth and scientific-exchange, not promotion. Often at academic/reference centers.
likes: Deep primary data, congress presence, publications
dislikes: Being treated as a volume target
dos: Engage via medical affairs, keep commercial separated (compliance)
Lead with the full evidence base and mechanism
donts: Don't push branded promo through scientific channels

hcp_segments.name: Community / time-poor generalist
hcp_segments.description: High patient throughput, minimal time; needs fast, practical, actionable guidance. Common in primary care and community oncology/cardiology.
dos: Provide ready-to-use patient materials and access support

hcp_segments.name: Evidence skeptic / late adopter
hcp_segments.description: Slow to change practice; wants robust outcomes, real-world evidence and peer validation before adopting. Low baseline engagement.
dos: Lead with durability, safety and guideline status
Be patient -- nurture over many touches

patient_caregiver_segments.name: Activated / self-advocating patient
likes: Detailed treatment info, trial finders, communities
Digital tracking tools and copay/access help

patient_caregiver_segments.name: Caregiver / care partner
likes: Practical caregiving guidance, logistics, adherence tools
dislikes: Being overlooked as a decision influencer

patient_caregiver_segments.name: Adherence-risk / disengaged patient
likes: Simple reminders, refill/copay help, low-effort nudges

cross_cutting_principles: Segment by behaviour and engagement signals, not just specialty/decile; cohorts should update dynamically as new Rx/engagement data arrive.
Right channel, right HCP, right moment -- omnichannel means orchestration, not every channel at once.
One message architecture across PP (personal promotion) and NPP (non-personal promotion); reinforce, never contradict, across channels.
Personalize: ~8 in 10 HCPs value tailored content and ~73% engage more when it is relevant to their patients/specialty.
Respect frequency and suppression: repetitive cross-channel outreach is the top driver of disengagement.
Keep medical (MSL/scientific exchange) and commercial promotion separated for KOL/academic audiences (compliance).
Lead unbranded/educational for newly diagnosed patients; reserve branded claims for activated, informed audiences.

Match channel weight to lifecycle stage: launch = awareness + PP-heavy education; growth = orchestrated PP+NPP conversion; mature = efficient defense/adherence; LOE = minimal acquisition, protect adherent base.
